messages.text: Leclerc takes blame for Hamilton clash at Monza after Ferrari talks

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc has admitted "I didn't behave the way I should have" when racing Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Charles Leclerc takes blame for Lewis Hamilton clash at Monza after pair hold talks ahead of Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Charles Leclerc takes blame for Lewis Hamilton clash at Monza after pair hold talks ahead of Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held talks together with Ferrari's bosses after their incident last time out at Monza; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid at 12.30pm and 4pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 10 September 2026 16:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See the Madring circuit in its entirety as the safety car completes a lap around the new Madrid F1 track Charles Leclerc has admitted "I didn't behave the way I should have" when racing Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton accused the team of having "no rules" after he was forced wide by Leclerc at the exit of the first chicane, an incident which cost him six positions, and could only recover to sixth place at Ferrari's home event. Ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, both drivers discussed the incident with Ferrari chairman John Elkann, chief executive Benedetto Vigna and team principal Frederic Vasseur. messages.text: St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runner-by-runner guide

metadata.summary: As the United States Of America celebrates its 250th anniversary, so does the world’s oldest Classic race. How many sporting events last this long? Very few.
metadata.content: St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runner-by-runner guide | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runner-by-runner guide With the 250th instalment of the world's oldest Classic on the horizon, Sky Sports Racing's Mike Cattermole runs through every contender going to post on Town Moor at 3.35pm on Saturday; Watch the race live from Doncaster on Sky Sports Racing. Thursday 10 September 2026 15:54, UK Image: Scandinavia won the 2025 renewal of the St Leger As the United States Of America celebrates its 250th anniversary, so does the world’s oldest Classic race. How many sporting events last this long? Very few. So, who will take Saturday's special renewal of the Betfred St Leger? First of all, it's great to see the Derby winner, Christmas Day, lining up. Not all that many do the double, a fact that I appreciated early in my racing life when even the mighty Shergar could manage only fourth. In more recent years, Camelot just missed out on his Triple Crown attempt. Remember, the Leger is only a furlong and a half shorter than two miles but you still need speed as well as stamina to take it. Never Say Die, St Paddy, Nijinksy and Reference Point are the last four to have backed up here after Epsom, however, so good luck to Christmas Day. Leger tips! messages.text: Humphries: Opening up on mental health was best choice I ever made

metadata.summary: World No 2 Luke Humphries said his rise to the top of darts would never have been possible had he not opened up about his mental health struggles.
metadata.content: Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health helped him rise to the top of darts | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health helped him rise to the top of darts Luke Humphries has been hailed for opening up about his mental health issues; the world No 2 believes speaking about his struggles has helped him rise to the top of darts Thursday 10 September 2026 12:33, UK Image: Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health struggles helped him rise to the top of darts World No 2 Luke Humphries said his rise to the top of darts would never have been possible had he not opened up about his mental health struggles. Humphries, who has partnered with the Samaritans to mark World Suicide Prevention Day, was on the grind of the PDC Tour when he suffered an anxiety attack midway through a tournament in 2019 and considered quitting. He spoke openly about his troubles, and it had a positive impact on him as he surged to the top of the game, culminating in winning the 2024 World Championship title and becoming world No 1. "For me, the best thing I ever did was go and see a doctor and go and tell him my feelings," Humphries said in conversation with a Samaritans volunteer. Image: Humphries went on to win the 2024 PDC World Darts Championship title and became world No 1 "Look who I am now. I've achieved so much from doing that and I'm so glad I did.
